en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Great Wish-Fulfilling Jewel Wheel Ox-King Protector, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amogha by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying at Vārāṇasī in the Deer Park, for the sake of Ājñātakauṇḍinya.
When [the Buddha] turned the wheel of the Dharma of the Four Noble Truths for these five persons, there was a son of heaven in the assembly named Ox-King (Go-rāja-devaputra).
He rose from his seat, bowed with palms joined, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I possess a spirit-mantra that grants mastery over all things according to one's wishes and brings benefit to all sentient beings. I pray only that the World-Honored One..."
“Venerable One, out of compassion, please grant me leave; I now wish to recite a great divine mantra. At that time, the Buddha praised him, saying, “Excellent!
You may speak it quickly; I wish to hear it. Thereupon, the devaputra spoke the mantra, saying:
Oṃ siddhi siddhi raṃja raṃja namo ṛddhiga puṣṭiga āvaha āvaha cintāmaṇi svāhā. At that time, the Bhagavān,
having heard the recitation of this divine mantra, surveyed all things universally for the sake of the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings.
Therefore, he spoke these verses:
"All sentient beings in the world Are oppressed by various miseries of poverty.

Though they seek the means of subsistence, may there be merit for giving to all beings, Causing them to attain freedom from sorrow and affliction. The power of this artifice surpasses that of all beasts."
Out of compassion for all sentient beings, you bestow all manner of precious jewels and fulfill all their aspirations;
you are equal to the hosts of devas, possessing peerless power of merit and timeless majesty.
To the Bhagavān, the Sage Vijina, with a heart of joy, faith, and delight, we offer various kinds of incense and flowers.
With lamps, the four types of offerings, and so forth, he paid homage to the deity Gośṛṅga-maniratna and spoke these verses: "Obeisance to the deity Gośṛṅga-maniratna, the divine beast!
I offer you fragrant unguents, flower garlands, and incense, Lamps, food and drink, and wealth in coin and silk.
Please accept these offerings with joy, and may your power increase!"
With majestic power and supernormal faculties pervading all forms, he manifests various colors and bestows all manner of treasures upon all classes of sentient beings.
Therefore, I make offerings to the Deity of the Divine Beast and, furthermore, to the Deity of the Cow-King Jewel.
Then, the Deity of the Cow-King Jewel addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, if there are any sons or daughters of good family..."
"Regarding those who uphold this sutra, how great a mass of merit do they obtain? Having been asked this, the Buddha told Gopāla-maṇi:

"The mass of merit possessed by those sons and daughters of good family from the first generation of the mind of awakening until their attainment of Buddhahood—the mass of merit of those individuals is equal to that [of one who upholds this scripture]. It should be known thus."
Noble sons and noble daughters are born from the mouth of the Tathāgata as children of the Buddha-mind.
Wherever such noble sons and noble daughters reside, that very place becomes a site where the Buddha performs his buddha-activities.
Therefore, if you wish to destroy the armies of Māra and bring benefit and happiness to all beings, and if you desire to attain the true wisdom of all Tathāgatas, [you should do so].
Such a person should single-mindedly read and recite this sutra; they will be able to swiftly accomplish all merits and virtues.
Furthermore, there are five kinds of miraculous efficacy regarding its title. What are these five? First, the person who upholds it can crush the hosts of Māra’s armies.
Second, the person who reads and recites it will obtain immeasurable merit and virtue in both this life and future lives. Third, the person who transcribes and makes offerings to it...
Nurturing others, one shall attain the eradication of offenses committed over immeasurable billions of kalpas in both this life and future lives, reaching the stage of Abhirati.
Fourth, all sufferings of illness shall be eliminated and one’s lifespan shall be extended.
Fifth, one shall obtain a portion of this precious jewel; those who provide offerings, perform sacrifices, recite, and show reverence will, in birth after birth, transform all...

The retribution of poverty and suffering can cause one to obtain the fruit of the inexhaustible secret treasury. At that time, when the Buddha had finished preaching this Sūtra of Divine Mantras, the entire assembly was filled with great joy;
they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The *Buddhabhāṣita-mahācintāmaṇi-go-rāja-rakṣā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
Completed on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month of the second year of the Yuansheng era, transcribed from the original manuscript obtained by Kuai Xuan.
Dedicated for the benefit of the mind of Vajrasena.
This book is an ancient manuscript preserved in the Seibon of Shinpuku-ji Temple at the southern end of the city,
which was transmitted by Prince Nin’yu of Hōshinnō lineage.
